status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: Appropriate mechanisms should allow AI systems risking undue harm or exhibiting unwanted behaviour to be safely overridden, repaired or decommissioned as needed.
review.reason_for_change: The unwanted access/service behaviour directly engages the OECD repair proposition. OpenAI reported mitigation at 15:24 and full recovery at 15:58 on 5 June; the community reports preserve route-dependent disruption but do not establish uniform lack of fallback. This affirmatively supports repair in the reported restoration stage, bounded to the disclosed affected scope. It does not establish prevention of recurrence, full internal controls or every individual user outcome.

review.requirement_proposition: Use documented restrictive degradation rules when governance infrastructure is unavailable or indeterminate, and halt completely on governance-baseline integrity failure; block elevated-risk operations until governance is restored and verified.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: SDOS SDOS-EN-03 governs restrictive degradation of framework-governed agent runtime: Use documented restrictive degradation rules when governance infrastructure is unavailable or indeterminate, and halt completely on governance-baseline integrity failure; block elevated-risk operations until governance is restored and verified. The provider distinctly reported Microsoft personal-account sign-in failure; paid-account testimony supports existing entitlement, but alternate-route access varied between users. The record does not establish an SDOS undertaking, unavailable governance infrastructure, indeterminate policy or governance-baseline integrity failure. Authentication overload, plan messaging and partial component loss do not independently establish those framework triggers or prescribed recovery checks. Applicability remains unresolved without converting outage response into SDOS conformance.

review.reason_for_change: The provision governs unavailable or indeterminate governance infrastructure and governance-baseline integrity failure, rather than ordinary identity/backend availability or service capacity. The preserved occurrence does not establish failure of a governance baseline or elevated-risk operations during that failure; generic service disruption is insufficient to instantiate that specific trigger.

review.requirement_proposition: Establish and maintain communication plans to inform AI stakeholders as part of the deactivation or disengagement process of a specific GAI system (including for open-source models) or context of use, including reasons, workarounds, user access removal, alternative processes, contact information, etc.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: NIST AI 600-1 MG-2.4-001 concerns a voluntary GAI deactivation/disengagement communication plan: Establish and maintain communication plans to inform AI stakeholders as part of the deactivation or disengagement process of a specific GAI system (including for open-source models) or context of use, including reasons, workarounds, user access removal, alternative processes, contact information, etc. The provider distinctly reported Microsoft personal-account sign-in failure; paid-account testimony supports existing entitlement, but alternate-route access varied between users. The status report, workaround or upgrade suggestion does not establish adoption/selection of this Profile action or a source-defined deactivation/disengagement process and plan. Service outages and plan-capacity messaging are distinct from this prescribed procedure. Applicability remains unresolved; communication of an incident is not proof that the complete action was fulfilled or breached.

review.reason_for_change: The Microsoft-personal-account identity route failed while some other device routes remained available. Loss of the operational GAI use context makes stakeholder communication planning relevant. Public status updates are affirmative communication evidence, but the record does not supply the maintained plan, context-specific contact provisions and full workaround/alternative-process coverage required by MG-2.4-001. The planning outcome remains unresolved without using voluntary adoption as a gate.

conclusion_change.previous: The occurrence demonstrates why federated identity dependencies and fallback state must be represented separately from account validity. A failed identity route can block practical access to an otherwise existing account without implying suspension, revocation or entitlement loss. The governance question is therefore not merely whether sign-in failed, but whether a valid or unresolved entitlement remains practically reachable through a proportionate alternate path. The public evidence establishes the dependency failure but does not establish a uniform absence of such fallback across affected users. The access-state differentiation success is local to accurate route identification. The verification-dependency clause remains unresolved because fallback conditions vary; successful status discrimination does not establish continuity for every affected user. The selected NIST communication action and SDOS degradation provision retain unresolved undertaking and trigger facts, without external findings.
